Andhra Pradesh.name: Andhra Pradesh

geography.physiography: Coastal plain (Circar Coast) and Rayalaseema plateau
geography.climate: Tropical monsoonal

tigerReserves: Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (India's largest by area)

examFacts: First state formed on linguistic basis in independent India (1 October 1953) following Potti Sreeramulu's hunger strike.
Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve is the largest tiger reserve in India by total area (3,728 sq km).
Kolleru Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in India, located between the Godavari and Krishna deltas.
Mangampet in Kadapa district holds over 90% of India's recoverable barytes reserves.
Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC SHAR) at Sriharikota in Tirupati district is ISRO's primary orbital launch facility.

Arunachal Pradesh.name: Arunachal Pradesh

geography.physiography: High mountain terrain ranging from Sub-Himalayan foothills to Greater Himalayas
geography.climate: Subtropical to Alpine

examFacts: Known as the 'Land of the Dawn-Lit Mountains'; Dong village in Anjaw district witnesses the earliest sunrise in India.
Namdapha National Park is renowned for harboring four big cat species: Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Clouded Leopard.
The McMahon Line demarcates the boundary between Arunachal Pradesh and China's Tibetan Plateau.
Apatani tribal community of Ziro Valley practices zero-waste agriculture integrating wet-rice farming with fish rearing.
Tawang Monastery, founded by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso in 1680–81, is the second-largest Buddhist monastery in the world.
sources: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region

Assam.name: Assam

geography.physiography: Brahmaputra Valley, Barak Valley, and intervening Karbi-Barail plateaus
geography.climate: Tropical monsoon climate with high humidity

majorMinerals: Petroleum (Digboi - oldest operating refinery in Asia)

classicalFolkDances: Sattriya (Classical dance created by Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev)

examFacts: Digboi is Asia's oldest operating oil refinery and has the world's oldest continually producing oil well (drilled 1889-1901).
Majuli in the Brahmaputra River was declared the first river island district of India in 2016.
Moidams of Charaideo (royal burial mounds of the Ahom dynasty) were inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage site in 2024.
Kaziranga National Park hosts around two-thirds of the world's total population of the Great One-Horned Rhinoceros.
Sattriya dance is one of the eight classical dances of India, initiated in the 15th century by Srimanta Sankardev in Assam's Vaishnavite monasteries (Sattras).

Bihar.name: Bihar
Bihar.formationDate: 22 March 1912 (separated from Bengal Presidency, State on 26 Jan 1950)

majorRivers: Ganga (divides state into north and south)
mountainsHills: Someshwar Range (foothills of Shivaliks in West Champaran)
geography.physiography: Flat fertile alluvial plain of the Middle Ganga Basin
geography.climate: Humid subtropical monsoon

historicalKingdoms: Magadha Empire (Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda, Mauryan, Sunga, Gupta dynasties)
Vajji Confederacy (world's earliest republic at Vaishali)
festivals: Sonepur Cattle Fair (Asia's largest cattle fair)
unescoSites: Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya (2002)

keySpecies: Gangetic Dolphin (National Aquatic Animal, Vikramshila Sanctuary)

examFacts: Vaishali is recognized as the world's first known democratic republic under the Lichchhavis during the 6th century BCE.
Nalanda Mahavihara was an ancient international university flourishing from the 5th century CE under the Guptas until destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji in c. 1193 CE.
Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary in Bhagalpur district is India's only dedicated protected area for the endangered Gangetic dolphin.
Champaran Satyagraha (1917) led by Mahatma Gandhi was his first Civil Disobedience movement in India against the exploitative Tinkathia indigo system.
Barabar Caves in Jehanabad district contain the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dedicated by Emperor Ashoka to Ajivika ascetics.

Chhattisgarh.name: Chhattisgarh

geography.physiography: Central Chhattisgarh Plain ('Rice Bowl of Central India') flanked by northern hills and southern Bastar plateau
geography.climate: Tropical wet and dry

majorMinerals: Iron Ore (Bailadila - exported to Japan via Vizag)
majorIndustries: Steel (Bhilai Steel Plant - SAIL, established with Soviet aid)

festivals: Bastar Dussehra (celebrated for 75 days, longest Dussehra)

keySpecies: Wild Water Buffalo (State Animal - Bubalus arnee)
Hill Myna (State Bird - Gracula religiosa peninsularis)

examFacts: Chhattisgarh is the sole commercial producer of tin ore (cassiterite) in India, concentrated in the Dantewada and Bastar districts.
Bailadila iron ore deposit contains one of the world's richest hematite iron ore bodies with iron content up to 66-68%.
Bhitarkanika and Bastar host rich indigenous heritage; Bastar Dussehra is unique because it worships Goddess Danteshwari instead of Rama's victory over Ravana.
Sirpur on the banks of Mahanadi was an ancient Buddhist, Shaivite and Vaishnavite cosmopolitan centre visited by Chinese traveler Xuanzang in 639 CE.
Chitrakote Falls on the Indravati River in Bastar district is known as the 'Niagara Falls of India' due to its horseshoe shape and immense monsoon width.

Goa.name: Goa

geography.physiography: Narrow Konkan coastal plain backed by the Western Ghats escarpment
geography.climate: Tropical monsoon

majorPortsPower: Mormugao Port (Major Port, premier iron ore exporter)

majorMonuments: Basilica of Bom Jesus (contains relics of St. Francis Xavier)
festivals: Sao Joao (festival of fertility and wells)

examFacts: Operation Vijay was launched on 18–19 December 1961 by the Indian Armed Forces to liberate Goa, Daman, and Diu from 451 years of Portuguese rule.
Goa is the smallest state of India by geographic area (3,702 sq km) and the fourth smallest by population.
Goa is the only Indian state that has continuously operated a Uniform Civil Code (Portuguese Civil Code of 1867) applicable to all citizens regardless of religion.
Dudhsagar Falls ('Sea of Milk') on the Mandovi River is a four-tiered waterfall located on the Goa-Karnataka border in Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary.
Goan Feni was the first product in India to receive a Geographical Indication (GI) tag under the specialty alcoholic beverage category.

Gujarat.name: Gujarat
Gujarat.formationDate: 1 May 1960 (bifurcation of Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat)

mountainsHills: Girnar Hills (Gorakhnath peak, 1,117 m - highest in Gujarat)
geography.physiography: Kathiawar Peninsula (Saurashtra), Great & Little Rann of Kutch, and mainland alluvial coastal plains
geography.climate: Arid to semi-arid in Kutch/Saurashtra, sub-humid in south Gujarat

majorMinerals: Petroleum and natural gas (Ankleshwar, Kalol, Cambay Basin)
majorIndustries: Petroleum refining (Jamnagar - Reliance, world's largest refining hub)

majorMonuments: Rani ki Vav (The Queen's Stepwell, Patan)
Statue of Unity (182 m, Kevadia - tallest statue in the world)

nationalParks: Marine National Park (Gulf of Kutch - India's 1st Marine NP)
keySpecies: Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica - sole wild habitat in the world)
Indian Wild Ass (Ghudkhur - Little Rann of Kutch)

examFacts: Gujarat possesses the longest coastline of any Indian state at approximately 1,600 km (nearly 24% of India's mainland coastline).
Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary in Saurashtra is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in the wild globally.

Dholavira in Kutch is the first Harappan site in India to be inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021), noted for its unique tripartite city plan and sophisticated stormwater harvesting reservoirs.
Lothal was a major port of the Indus Valley Civilization featuring the world's earliest known tidal dockyard connected to the Sabarmati river channel.
The Statue of Unity, depicting Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at Kevadia on the Narmada River, stands 182 meters tall, making it the tallest statue in the world.

Haryana.name: Haryana
Haryana.formationDate: 1 November 1966 (carved out of East Punjab on recommendation of Shah Commission)

mountainsHills: Shivalik Hills (northeast - Karoh Peak 1,467 m in Morni Hills)
geography.physiography: Indo-Gangetic alluvial plain, semi-arid sandy plains of Bagar, and Shivalik-Morni foothills
geography.climate: Semi-arid to sub-tropical continental

majorIndustries: Automobiles (Maruti Suzuki - Gurugram & Manesar, largest car manufacturer)
majorPortsPower: Gorakhpur Atomic Power Project (Fatehabad - under construction)

majorMonuments: Rakhigarhi (largest Harappan site in the subcontinent)
classicalFolkDances: Dhamal (ancient martial folk dance dating to Mahabharata era)

examFacts: Rakhigarhi in Hisar district has been established as the largest archaeological site of the Indus Valley Civilization, spanning over 350 hectares.
Panipat was the site of three epoch-defining battles in Indian history: 1526 (Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi), 1556 (Akbar defeated Hemu), and 1761 (Ahmad Shah Durrani defeated Marathas).
Kurukshetra is the legendary battlefield of the Mahabharata where Lord Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna at Jyotisar.
Haryana has the lowest forest cover percentage among Indian states according to the India State of Forest Report (ISFR).
The Shah Commission (1966) recommended the division of the erstwhile Punjab state on linguistic lines, creating Haryana on 1 November 1966.

Himachal Pradesh.name: Himachal Pradesh

mountainsHills: Zanskar Range (Reo Purgyil - highest peak, 6,816 m)
geography.physiography: Extremely mountainous, transitioning from sub-tropical foothills to perennially glaciated peaks and trans-Himalayan rain-shadow deserts (Spiti)
majorLakes: Renuka Lake (Ramsar - largest natural lake in HP)
Pong Dam Lake (Maharana Pratap Sagar - Ramsar)
geography.climate: Subtropical in southern tracts to Alpine and cold desert in Spiti and Lahaul

majorCrops: Apples ('Apple State of India' - Kotgarh, Shimla, Kinnaur)
majorMinerals: Rock salt (Gumma and Drang in Mandi - unique in India)
majorIndustries: Pharmaceutical manufacturing (Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh hub - Asia's largest pharma cluster)

majorMonuments: Kangra Fort (oldest dated fort in India)
Tabo Monastery ('Ajanta of the Himalayas', founded 996 CE)
classicalFolkDances: Nati (Guinness World Record for largest folk dance)
festivals: Kullu Dussehra (commences when Dussehra ends elsewhere)
unescoSites: Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area (2014)

nationalParks: Pin Valley National Park (cold desert biosphere)

examFacts: The Kalka-Shimla Railway, constructed under British rule in 1903, features 103 tunnels and over 800 bridges, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Tabo Monastery in the Spiti Valley, established in 996 CE by the Buddhist translator Rinchen Zangpo, is celebrated as the oldest continuously functioning Buddhist enclave in India.
Atal Tunnel under the Rohtang Pass, spanning 9.02 km at an altitude over 3,000 meters, is one of the world's longest single-tube highway tunnels above 10,000 feet.
Renuka Lake in Sirmaur district is a Ramsar wetland named after Renuka, mother of Parashurama, shaped like a reclining woman.
Baddi in Solan district manufactures approximately 35% of all pharmaceutical formulations produced in Asia.

Jharkhand.name: Jharkhand
Jharkhand.formationDate: 15 November 2000 (birth anniversary of Birsa Munda, separated from Bihar)

mountainsHills: Parasnath Hills (Shikharji - 1,365 m, highest peak in Jharkhand)
Rajmahal Hills (famous for Jurassic plant fossils)
geography.physiography: Chota Nagpur Plateau, composed of Ranchi, Hazaribagh, and Koderma plateaus with Patlands
geography.climate: Humid subtropical with distinct seasonal variations

majorMinerals: Coal (Jharia - premier prime coking coal field in India)
Iron Ore (Noamundi, Chiria - largest single iron ore deposit)
majorIndustries: Steel (Tata Steel / TISCO at Jamshedpur - India's 1st private steel plant; Bokaro Steel Plant - SAIL)
majorPortsPower: Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC - India's 1st multipurpose river valley project, 1948)

classicalFolkDances: Chhau Dance (Seraikella Chhau - UNESCO Intangible Heritage)
festivals: Sarhul (worship of Sal tree / spring festival)
Sohrai and Khovar (harvest and mural art)
giTaggedProducts: Sohrai Khovar Painting (Hazaribagh - traditional mural art)

tigerReserves: Palamu Tiger Reserve (one of the original 9 Project Tiger reserves of 1973)

examFacts: Jharkhand accounts for more than 40% of the mineral reserves of India, earning the Chota Nagpur Plateau the title of the 'Ruhr of India'.
Jaduguda in East Singhbhum district was the first uranium mine discovered and operated in India (1967) by the Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL).
Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), modeled on America's Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), was established on 7 July 1948 as independent India's first multipurpose river valley project.
Parasnath Hill (Shikharji) is the most sacred pilgrimage site for Jains, where 20 of the 24 Tirthankaras attained Nirvana.
Subarnarekha River is historically significant as gold particles were panned from its river sands, and Hundru Falls is formed on its course near Ranchi.

Karnataka.name: Karnataka
Karnataka.formationDate: 1 November 1956 (State of Mysore; renamed Karnataka on 1 Nov 1973)

mountainsHills: Mullayanagiri (highest peak in Karnataka, 1,930 m in Baba Budan Giri)
geography.physiography: Coastal plain (Canara), Western Ghats (Malnad), and Deccan plateau (Bayaluseeme: North & South Maidan)
majorLakes: Shanthi Sagara (second largest artificial lake in Asia)
geography.climate: Tropical monsoon on coast to semi-arid in northern interior

majorCrops: Coffee (>70% of India's coffee - Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru, Hassan)
majorMinerals: Gold (Kolar Gold Fields - KGF, and Hutti Gold Mines - only active gold mine in India)
majorIndustries: Information Technology ('Silicon Valley of India' - Bengaluru)
Aerospace and Defence (HAL, ISRO, DRDO labs)
majorPortsPower: Pavagada Solar Park (one of the world's largest solar parks)

historicalKingdoms: Kingdom of Mysore (Wodeyars, Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan)
majorMonuments: Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura)

keySpecies: Asian Elephant (State Animal - Karnataka has the largest elephant population in India)
Bengal Tiger (second highest population in India)

examFacts: Hutti Gold Mines in Raichur district is currently the only active primary gold-producing mine in India.
The Hoysala Temples of Belur, Halebidu, and Somanathapura were inscribed as India's 42nd UNESCO World Heritage Site in September 2023.
Jog Falls (Gersoppa Falls) on the Sharavathi River in Shivamogga district drops 253 meters in four distinct cascades named Raja, Roarer, Rocket, and Rani.
Gommateshwara (Bahubali) statue at Shravanabelagola, carved out of a single granite block in 981 CE under Western Ganga minister Chavundaraya, is one of the world's largest monolithic statues.
Baba Budan Giri in Chikkamagaluru is the cradle of coffee cultivation in India, where Sufi saint Baba Budan smuggled seven raw coffee beans from Yemen in the 17th century.

Kerala.name: Kerala
Kerala.formationDate: 1 November 1956 (States Reorganisation Act, merging Travancore-Cochin and Malabar)

mountainsHills: Anamudi (2,695 m - highest peak in Peninsular India / south of Himalayas)
geography.physiography: Three distinct physiographic zones: Highlands (Western Ghats), Midlands (hills and valleys), and Lowlands (coastal belt and backwaters)
majorLakes: Vembanad Lake (longest lake in India and largest Ramsar wetland in Kerala)
Sasthamcotta Lake (largest freshwater lake in Kerala)
geography.climate: Tropical maritime monsoon with two monsoons (South-West and North-East)

majorMinerals: Heavy mineral beach sands (Monazite - rich in thorium, Ilmenite, Rutile, Zircon at Chavara/Alappuzha coast)
majorPortsPower: Cochin Port (Major Port with Vallarpadam International Container Transshipment Terminal)
Vizhinjam International Seaport (India's premier deepwater transshipment hub)

historicalKingdoms: Kingdom of Travancore (Marthanda Varma - Battle of Colachel 1741)
majorMonuments: St. Francis Church (Kochi - original burial place of Vasco da Gama)
classicalFolkDances: Koodiyattam (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage - ancient Sanskrit theatre)
festivals: Thrissur Pooram (festival of percussion and caparisoned elephants)

nationalParks: Eravikulam National Park (Munnar - home of Nilgiri Tahr and Neelakurinji)
Silent Valley National Park (Palakkad - pristine rainforest)
keySpecies: Nilgai Tahr (State Animal - Eravikulam holds the largest population)

examFacts: Anamudi Peak (2,695 m) in Eravikulam National Park, Idukki district, is the highest mountain peak in Peninsular India and all of India south of the Himalayas.

Kuttanad region in Alappuzha and Kottayam districts is renowned as the only place in India where farming is successfully conducted 1.2 to 3 meters below sea level (recognized by FAO as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System - GIAHS).
Battle of Colachel (1741): King Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeated the Dutch East India Company, marking the first time an Asian kingdom routed a European naval power in Indian waters.
Silent Valley National Park was saved from a hydroelectric project following the landmark 'Save Silent Valley' ecological movement (1970s–1980s), pioneering modern Indian environmental jurisprudence.
Cochin Shipyard built INS Vikrant, India's first indigenously designed and manufactured aircraft carrier (IAC-1), commissioned in September 2022.

Madhya Pradesh.name: Madhya Pradesh

majorRivers: Narmada (flows westward in a rift valley)
mountainsHills: Mahadeo Hills (Dhupgarh - 1,350 m, highest peak in MP in Pachmarhi)
geography.physiography: Central Highlands, Malwa Plateau, Narmada-Son Trough, Satpura-Maikal Range, and Bundelkhand/Baghelkhand plateaus
majorLakes: Bhoj Wetland (Bada Talab and Chhota Talab, Bhopal - Ramsar site)
geography.climate: Subtropical with hot dry summers and mild winters
soilTypes: Black cotton soil (covers Malwa and Narmada valley)

majorMinerals: Diamond (Majhgawan mine in Panna - sole diamond producing mine in India)
Copper (Malanjkhand in Balaghat - largest open-cast copper deposit in India)
majorIndustries: Automobile testing and assembly (Pithampur - 'Detroit of India')

majorMonuments: Gwalior Fort ('Pearl of the fortresses of Hind')
festivals: Simhastha Kumbh Mela (Ujjain, on Kshipra river every 12 years)
unescoSites: Gwalior and Orchha (Historic Urban Landscape initiative)
giTaggedProducts: Bell Metal Ware of Datia and Tikamgarh

keySpecies: Bengal Tiger ('Tiger State of India' - highest tiger census count)
Barasingha / Hard-ground Swamp Deer (State Animal - Kanha mascot 'Bhoorsingh')
African Cheetah (reintroduced in Kuno NP, September 2022)

examFacts: Madhya Pradesh holds the largest forest area by total square kilometers in India (77,493 sq km, ISFR 2021).
Panna district is the sole active producer of diamonds in India, operated by the National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) at Majhgawan.
Project Cheetah, the world's first intercontinental large-carnivore translocation project, reintroduced African cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa to Kuno National Park in September 2022.
Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka in Raisen district contain over 750 rock shelters showcasing unbroken human artistic expression from Upper Paleolithic to Mesolithic and historic periods.
The Ken-Betwa River Link Project is India's first river interlinking project implemented under the National Perspective Plan to transfer surplus water from Ken to drought-prone Bundelkhand.

Maharashtra.name: Maharashtra
Maharashtra.formationDate: 1 May 1960 (Bombay State reorganization under Samyukta Maharashtra Movement)
neighboringStates: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

administrativeDivisions.highCourt: Bombay High Court (Benches at Nagpur, Aurangabad, Panaji)

majorRivers: Godavari (Dakshin Ganga - originates at Trimbakeshwar, Nashik)
geography.physiography: Konkan coastal strip, Western Ghats escarpment, and the vast Deccan Lava Plateau (composed of thick basaltic Deccan Traps)
majorLakes: Lonar Lake (meteorite impact crater lake - Ramsar site)
geography.climate: Tropical monsoon on coast to dry semi-arid in the rain-shadow Marathwada/Vidarbha
soilTypes: Black cotton soil (Regur - weathered basalt, ideal for cotton)

majorCrops: Onions (Lasalgaon - largest onion market in Asia)
majorIndustries: Financial and Banking Capital of India (Mumbai - RBI, BSE, NSE, SEBI)
majorPortsPower: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA / Nhava Sheva - largest container port in India)
Tarapur Atomic Power Station (India's first commercial nuclear power plant, 1969)
Koyna Hydroelectric Project (1,960 MW - largest completed HEP in Maharashtra)

majorMonuments: Ajanta Caves (monolithic Buddhist rock-cut monasteries, 2nd century BCE to 5th century CE)
Ellora Caves (Kailasa Temple - Cave 16, largest monolithic rock excavation in the world)
Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai
classicalFolkDances: Lavani (traditional folk dance accompanied by Dholki)
festivals: Ganeshotsav (revitalized by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1893 as a public festival)
unescoSites: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai (2018)

nationalParks: Sanjay Gandhi National Park (Borivali, Mumbai - unique NP within a megacity)
tigerReserves: Bor Tiger Reserve (smallest tiger reserve by core area)
keySpecies: Indian Giant Squirrel (Shekru - State Animal, Bhimashankar Sanctuary)

examFacts: Lonar Lake in Buldhana district is an internationally renowned hyper-saline, soda lake created by a meteorite collision impact approximately 50,000 years ago during the Pleistocene epoch.
The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) at Ellora was carved vertically downwards out of a single monolithic basalt rock cliff face under Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century CE.
Tarapur Atomic Power Station (TAPS) in Palghar district, commissioned in October 1969 with boiling water reactors (BWR), is the oldest commercial nuclear power station in India.
Mumbai High (formerly Bombay High), situated 160 km off the Mumbai coast in the Arabian Sea, is India's most productive offshore oilfield, discovered in 1974 by ONGC's drillship Sagar Samrat.

Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti led the movement that achieved the creation of the Marathi-speaking state of Maharashtra on 1 May 1960 with Mumbai as its capital, following the bifurcation of bilingual Bombay State.

Odisha.name: Odisha
Odisha.formationDate: 1 April 1936 (Utkal Divas, separated from Bihar and Orissa Province)

mountainsHills: Deomali (highest peak in Odisha, 1,672 m in Koraput)
geography.physiography: Coastal Plains (Hexadeltaic region), Central River Basins, Eastern Ghats highlands, and Western undulating plateaus
majorLakes: Chilika Lake (largest brackish water lagoon in Asia and India's 1st Ramsar site)
geography.climate: Tropical savanna with frequent Bay of Bengal cyclonic storms

majorMinerals: Iron Ore (Keonjhar, Sundargarh, Mayurbhanj - largest producer in India)
Bauxite (Kalahandi, Rayagada, Koraput - >50% of India's bauxite)
Chromite (Sukinda Valley, Jajpur - >95% of India's chromite)
majorIndustries: Steel (Rourkela Steel Plant - India's 1st public sector plant with German aid, Jindal Steel, Tata Steel Kalinganagar)
Aluminium (NALCO Damanjodi & Angul, Vedanta Jharsuguda - India's aluminium capital)
majorPortsPower: Paradip Port (Major Port - deepwater port, leading cargo handler)

historicalKingdoms: Kalinga (Kalinga War of 261 BCE - transformed Ashoka to Buddhism)
Mahameghavahana Dynasty (Emperor Kharavela of Hathigumpha inscription)
Eastern Ganga Dynasty (built Konark Sun Temple & Puri Jagannath Temple)
classicalFolkDances: Odissi (Classical dance - codified in Natya Shastra, revived by Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra)
festivals: Raja Parba (celebrating womanhood and mother earth)
Boita Bandana (Bali Jatra at Cuttack - ancient maritime trade with Southeast Asia)
Dhanu Jatra (Bargarh - world's largest open-air theatre)
giTaggedProducts: Similipal Kai Chutney (red weaver ant chutney)

nationalParks: Similipal National Park (Biosphere Reserve, Tiger Reserve, Elephant Reserve)
Bhitarkanika National Park (mangrove ecosystem, saltwater crocodiles)
tigerReserves: Similipal Tiger Reserve (noted for unique melanistic / black tigers)
keySpecies: Olive Ridley Sea Turtle (Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary & Rushikulya rookery - world's largest mass nesting/arribada site)

examFacts: The Kalinga War fought on the banks of the Daya River near Dhauli in 261 BCE resulted in profound devastation, compelling Mauryan Emperor Ashoka to renounce military conquest (Digvijaya) in favor of cultural/moral conquest (Dhammavijaya).

Chilika Lake was the first Indian wetland of international importance designated under the Ramsar Convention on 1 October 1981, and successfully removed from the Montreux Record following eco-restoration in 2002.
Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary in Kendrapara district is recognized as the world's largest rookery for the endangered Olive Ridley sea turtle, hosting millions during annual mass nestings (Arribada).
Hirakud Dam across the Mahanadi River near Sambalpur, inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1957, is one of the longest earthen dams in the world (main section 4.8 km, total dyke length 25.8 km).
Similipal Tiger Reserve is globally unique for harboring wild melanistic (black) tigers, possessing pseudo-melanism caused by a rare mutation in the Transmembrane Aminopeptidase Q (Taqpep) gene.

Punjab.name: Punjab
Punjab.formationDate: 1 November 1966 (present boundaries; historic state split in 1947 Partition)

majorRivers: Beas (only Indus river flowing entirely in India)
mountainsHills: Shivalik Hills (northeast foothills - Dhar Kalan, Ropar, Hoshiarpur)
geography.physiography: Extremely fertile alluvial plains divided into three cultural-geographic regions: Majha (between Ravi and Beas), Doaba (between Beas and Sutlej), and Malwa (south of Sutlej)
majorLakes: Harike Wetland (confluence of Beas and Sutlej - Ramsar site)
geography.climate: Subtropical with extreme hot summers and cold winters with frost

majorPortsPower: Guru Gobind Singh Super Thermal Power (Ropar)

historicalKingdoms: Sikh Confederacy (Misls) and Sikh Empire (Maharaja Ranjit Singh)
majorMonuments: Qila Mubarak (Bathinda - where Razia Sultana was imprisoned)
festivals: Baisakhi (commemorates creation of Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699 & harvest)
giTaggedProducts: Phulkari (traditional floral embroidery, shared with Haryana)

keySpecies: Indus River Dolphin (critically endangered - Beas River hosts the only wild population in India)

examFacts: Harike Wetland, situated at the confluence of the Beas and Sutlej rivers, is the source of the Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan Feeder), one of the longest canal systems in the world.
The Beas River Conservation Reserve is the only habitat in India harboring a wild population of the endangered Indus River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica minor).
Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred in Amritsar on Baisakhi, 13 April 1919, when British troops commanded by Colonel Reginald Dyer fired on an unarmed gathering protesting the Rowlatt Act.

Punjab served as the testing ground and epicenter of the Green Revolution in India during the 1960s, pioneered by Dr. M. S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug introducing semi-dwarf high-yielding wheat varieties (Kalyan Sona, Sonalika).
Anandpur Sahib was the site where the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, established the Khalsa Panth on Baisakhi Day in 1699.

Rajasthan.name: Rajasthan
Rajasthan.formationDate: 30 March 1949 (Rajasthan Day, unified from 19 princely states)
internationalBorders: Pakistan (longest state border with Pakistan, ~1,070 km along Radcliffe Line)

administrativeDivisions.highCourt: Rajasthan High Court (Principal seat at Jodhpur, Bench at Jaipur)

majorRivers: Chambal (only perennial river, famous for ravines/badland topography)
Banas (longest river flowing entirely within Rajasthan)
Luni (inland drainage into Rann of Kutch)
mountainsHills: Aravalli Range (oldest fold mountain range in India; Guru Shikhar - 1,722 m at Mount Abu is highest peak)
geography.physiography: Thar Desert (Marusthali and semi-arid Bagar west of Aravallis), Aravalli Mountain spine, Eastern Alluvial Plains, and Hadoti Plateau (southeast)
majorLakes: Sambhar Salt Lake (largest inland saline lake in India - Ramsar site)
geography.climate: Arid to semi-arid in the west; sub-humid in southeastern Hadoti

majorCrops: Mustard and Rapeseed (largest producer in India)
majorMinerals: Lead and Zinc (Zawar and Rampura Agucha - sole producer in India)
Marble and Granite (Makrana - built Taj Mahal)
Petroleum (Barmer Basin - Mangala, Bhagyam, Aishwarya oilfields)
majorIndustries: Solar energy (Bhadla Solar Park - world's largest solar park by capacity, ~2,245 MW)
majorPortsPower: Rawatbhata / Rajasthan Atomic Power Station (RAPS - heavy water reactors)

historicalKingdoms: Rajput Clans (Mewar / Sisodias, Marwar / Rathores, Amber / Kachhwahas, Bikaner, Haras of Bundi/Kota)
majorMonuments: Six Hill Forts of Rajasthan (Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber, Jaisalmer)
Jantar Mantar (Jaipur - astronomical observatory of Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II)
Dilwara Jain Temples (Mount Abu - marble carvings)
classicalFolkDances: Ghoomar (traditional dance of Bhil tribe & Rajput women)
Kalbelia (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage - serpent dance)

tigerReserves: Sariska Tiger Reserve (first reserve to successfully airlift & reintroduce tigers, 2008)
ramsarSites: Keoladeo Ghana National Park (1981, Montreux Record)
keySpecies: Great Indian Bustard (Godawan - State Bird, critically endangered)

examFacts: Rajasthan is the largest state of India by geographic area (342,239 sq km), accounting for 10.4% of the total geographic territory of the country.
Sambhar Salt Lake in Jaipur/Nagaur districts is India's largest inland saline lake and produces approximately 9% of the nation's salt.
The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest geological fold mountain systems in the world, dating to the Proterozoic eon, acting as a natural barrier checking eastward expansion of the Thar Desert.
Pokhran in Jaisalmer district was the test site for both of India's nuclear detonations: Operation Smiling Buddha on 18 May 1974 and Operation Shakti (Pokhran-II) on 11–13 May 1998.
Bhadla Solar Park in Phalodi/Jodhpur district is recognized as one of the largest solar parks in the world with an installed operational capacity exceeding 2,240 MW.
sources: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

Tamil Nadu.name: Tamil Nadu
Tamil Nadu.formationDate: 26 January 1950 (Madras State; renamed Tamil Nadu on 14 January 1969)
internationalBorders: Palk Strait maritime boundary with Sri Lanka

administrativeDivisions.highCourt: Madras High Court (Principal seat at Chennai, Bench at Madurai)

majorRivers: Kaveri (lifeline of Tamil Nadu - Mettur Dam)
mountainsHills: Eastern Ghats (Shevaroy Hills, Javadi Hills, Kalrayan Hills, Kolli Hills)
geography.physiography: Coromandel Coastal Plain, fertile Kaveri Delta, Western Ghats escarpment, and inland Deccan plateau uplands
geography.climate: Tropical maritime; receives maximum rainfall during North-East (Retreating) Monsoon (October-December)

majorIndustries: Textiles and Spinning Mills (Coimbatore - 'Manchester of South India', Tiruppur - 'Knitwear Capital')
Leather tanning and export (Vellore, Ambur, Ranipet)
Wind energy (Muppandal Wind Farm - largest operational onshore wind farm in India)
majorPortsPower: Kamarajar Port (Ennore - India's 1st corporatized major port)
Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant (India's largest nuclear plant, 2x1000 MW VVER)

historicalKingdoms: Sangam Era (Three Crowned Kings - Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas)
Imperial Cholas (Rajaraja Chola I & Rajendra Chola I)
majorMonuments: Great Living Chola Temples (Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Airavatesvara at Darasuram)
Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram (Shore Temple, Pancha Rathas, Arjuna's Penance)
classicalFolkDances: Bharatanatyam (India's oldest classical dance, codified in Natya Shastra)
unescoSites: Mountain Railways of India: Nilgiri Mountain Railway (2005)

nationalParks: Guindy National Park (Chennai - one of the few NPs located inside a city)
Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park (India's first marine biosphere reserve)
ramsarSites: Gulf of Mannar Marine Biosphere Reserve
Vedanthangal (oldest water bird sanctuary in India)
keySpecies: Dugong / Sea Cow (Gulf of Mannar Dugong Conservation Reserve)

examFacts: Tamil Nadu possesses the highest number of Ramsar Wetland sites of any state in India (16 Ramsar sites as of 2024).

Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tirunelveli district, developed in collaboration with Russia's Rosatom, has an ultimate planned capacity of 6,000 MW, making it the highest-capacity nuclear station in India.
Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, built by Rajaraja Chola I between 1003 and 1010 CE, features a vimana tower rising 66 meters topped by an 80-tonne monolithic granite cupola (kumbam).
Pamban Bridge, opened in 1914 connecting Rameswaram island on Pamban Island to mainland India, was India's first sea bridge, featuring a double-leaf bascule section designed by Scherzer.

Unlike most of India which receives primary precipitation from the South-West Monsoon (June–Sept), coastal Tamil Nadu receives ~50–60% of its annual precipitation from the North-East Retreating Monsoon (Oct–Dec).

Uttar Pradesh.name: Uttar Pradesh

administrativeDivisions.highCourt: Allahabad High Court (Principal seat at Prayagraj, Bench at Lucknow)

majorRivers: Yamuna (Triveni Sangam at Prayagraj with invisible Saraswati)
mountainsHills: Vindhyan Hills & Kaimur Range (southern edge in Mirzapur, Sonbhadra, Bundelkhand)
geography.physiography: Bhabhar and Terai belt in north, vast Gangetic Alluvial Plains (Doab, Rohilkhand, Awadh, Purvanchal), and Vindhyan plateaus/hills in south
majorLakes: Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar (Rihand Dam, Sonbhadra - largest man-made reservoir in India by volume)
geography.climate: Humid subtropical with profound seasonal variations
soilTypes: Bundelkhand red/black soils (Rakar, Parwa, Mar, Kabar)

majorCrops: Sugarcane ('Sugar Bowl of India' - largest producer)
majorIndustries: Leather manufacturing (Kanpur - 'Leather City of the World' and Agra)
IT and Electronics (Noida & Greater Noida - mobile handset manufacturing hub)
majorPortsPower: National Waterway 1 (NW-1 Ganga: Prayagraj to Haldia, multi-modal terminal at Varanasi)

historicalKingdoms: Mahajanapadas (8 of 16 were in UP: Kuru, Panchala, Kosala, Vatsa, Surasena, Chedi, Malla, Kashi)
Mughal Empire (Agra and Fatehpur Sikri capitals)
majorMonuments: Taj Mahal (Agra - white marble mausoleum built by Shah Jahan)
Fatehpur Sikri (Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal, Salim Chishti Dargah)
Sarnath (Dhamek Stupa - site of Buddha's First Sermon)
Kashi Vishwanath Temple (Varanasi - one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world)
classicalFolkDances: Kathak (sole Classical Dance of North India, nurtured in Lucknow Gharana)
festivals: Kumbh Mela / Maha Kumbh at Prayagraj (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage - world's largest religious gathering)

tigerReserves: Pilibhit Tiger Reserve (received inaugural TX2 international award)
keySpecies: Swamp Deer / Barasingha (State Animal - Dudhwa holds key population)
Sarus Crane (State Bird - world's tallest flying bird)

examFacts: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous administrative subdivision in the world with over 199.8 million inhabitants according to the 2011 Census.
Sarnath near Varanasi is where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta - 'Turning the Wheel of the Law') to his first five disciples.
The Revolt of 1857 ignited on 10 May 1857 at Meerut cantonment, preceded by Mangal Pandey's rebellion at Barrackpore.
Triveni Sangam at Prayagraj is the sacred confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and mythical Saraswati rivers, venue for the Kumbh Mela and Maha Kumbh.
Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar created by the Rihand Dam on the Rihand River in Sonbhadra district is India's largest artificial reservoir by total storage volume (~10.6 billion cubic meters).

West Bengal.name: West Bengal
internationalBorders: Bangladesh (longest international border of any Indian state, ~2,217 km)

administrativeDivisions.highCourt: Calcutta High Court (oldest High Court in India, established 1862)

majorRivers: Ganga / Bhagirathi-Hooghly (Farakka Barrage bifurcates Ganga into Padma and Hooghly)
mountainsHills: Eastern Himalayas (Darjeeling Hills - Sandakphu 3,636 m is the highest peak in West Bengal along Singalila Ridge)
Ayodhya Hills & Panchet Hills (Purulia plateau extension)
geography.physiography: Darjeeling Himalayan hill region, Terai-Dooars foothills, Northern plains, Rarh region, and Lower Gangetic Delta / Sundarbans
majorLakes: East Kolkata Wetlands (Ramsar - natural sewage treatment wetland)
geography.climate: Tropical monsoon in plains to temperate and alpine in Darjeeling hills
soilTypes: Laterite soil (Rarh region - Bankura, Purulia, Birbhum)

majorCrops: Paddy (largest rice producing state in India)
Jute ('Golden Fibre' - largest producer in India)
majorMinerals: Coal (Raniganj - birthplace of coal mining in India, 1774)
majorIndustries: Steel (Durgapur Steel Plant - SAIL, IISCO Burnpur)
Heavy engineering (Chittaranjan Locomotive Works - India's 1st locomotive builder)
Information Technology (Salt Lake Sector V, Rajarhat New Town)
majorPortsPower: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port / Kolkata Port (oldest operating major port in India and only riverine major port, with Haldia Dock Complex)

historicalKingdoms: Pala Empire (Dharmapala, Devapala - patrons of Buddhism)
British East India Company (Battle of Plassey 1757, Calcutta served as capital of British India until 1911)
majorMonuments: Howrah Bridge (Rabindra Setu - cantilever bridge over Hooghly)
classicalFolkDances: Purulia Chhau (vigorous martial mask dance - UNESCO Intangible Heritage)
Baul songs and dance (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage)
festivals: Durga Puja (inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2021)
Ganga Sagar Mela (Sagar Island - second largest gathering after Kumbh Mela)
unescoSites: Mountain Railways of India: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (1999)
giTaggedProducts: Darjeeling Tea (First product in India to receive a GI tag in 2004)

nationalParks: Jaldapara National Park (hosts 2nd largest population of one-horned rhinos in India)
tigerReserves: Sundarbans Tiger Reserve (only mangrove tiger habitat in the world)
ramsarSites: Sundarban Wetland (2019 - largest Ramsar site in India by surface area, 4,230 sq km)
keySpecies: Royal Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris tigris - swimming tigers of Sundarbans)

examFacts: Darjeeling Tea became the very first Geographical Indication (GI) tagged product of India in 2004–2005 under the GI Act of 1999.

Santiniketan in Birbhum district, founded by Maharshi Debendranath Tagore and expanded by Nobel Laureate Rabindranath Tagore into Visva-Bharati, was inscribed as India's 41st UNESCO World Heritage Site in September 2023.
Sundarbans Delta, formed by the confluence of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers, is the world's largest delta and hosts the largest contiguous mangrove forest globally.

Battle of Plassey took place on 23 June 1757 near Palashi on the Bhagirathi River, where Robert Clive's British forces defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah, establishing the foundation of British dominion in India.
Calcutta served as the capital of the British Raj in India from 1772 until King George V announced the transfer of the imperial capital to Delhi during the Delhi Durbar of 1911.
